newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian c.bank wants stable real exchange rate.
newsitem.headline: Russian c.bank wants stable real exchange rate.

text.p: The Russian central bank believes a stable real exchange rate is in the best interest of the economy and it will resist market forces encouraging a real appreciation of the rouble, a senior central banker said on Thursday.

Sergei Aleksashenko, the bank's first deputy chairman, told Reuters Financial Television the bank would stick to its policy of a gradual, pre-announced depreciation of the rouble within a currency corridor.

Separately, the bank issued a statement saying: "The Bank of Russia will continue the practical realisation of its policy of a slow movement...in the official rate, which corresponds to the realities of the economic situation."
Aleksashenko said current demand for roubles was partly due to seasonal factors and partly due to a general revival in economic activity.

The bank will counter the demand for roubles by widening the spread of the bid/offer rates it currently quotes every day in the currency market, he said. The rate at which it sells dollars will move down faster than the rate at which it buys dollars.
He said the current situation was similar to that in spring/summer 1995, when inflation outstripped the nominal depreciation of the rouble.

"The Bank of Russia does not believe it possible to allow a repetition of this kind of influence of market forces on the rouble rate, since it believes a currency policy aimed at maintaining the stability of the real exchange rate in relation to foreign currencies is correct and corresponds to the interests of the national economy," the statement said.
The central bank is continuing to intervene actively in the currency and government secruities markets, he said.
